problem: The gain-factor formulas are missing the exponent. '106.02/20', '10GM/20' and '108/20' read literally as (106.02/20), (10*GM/20) and (108/20), not 10^(6.02/20), 10^(GM/20) and 10^(8/20); the stated equalities to 2 and 2.51 are then false.
fix: Write the factors as 10^(6.02/20)=2, 10^(GM/20), and 10^(8/20)=2.51 (or use superscript tags).

problem: GM is not the geometric distance from the negative real-axis crossing to −1. For a crossing at −a (a>0), the gain margin is -20 log10(a) dB (allowable factor 1/a); the distance from the crossing to −1 is |1-a| and cannot carry the sign of GM.
fix: Define GM from the crossing magnitude: if the negative-real-axis crossing is at −a, GM=20 log10(1/a) dB for the stable case, with gain factor 1/a. Then describe PM as the angle between the negative real axis and the unit-circle crossing.

problem: The answer writes PM = 180° − 150° for a phase of −150°, which contradicts the trap that PM = 180° + phase. The number is right only because 150° is being used as the magnitude of the lag.
A closed-loop characteristic root on the jω-axis does not by itself make the closed loop marginally stable; other closed-loop poles can still be in the right half-plane.
fix: Say that −1 on the open-loop locus gives a closed-loop pole on the jω-axis; the closed loop is marginal only when all other closed-loop poles are in the left half-plane.

problem: 'The system still has a PM, read at its 0 dB crossing' is not always true. If the magnitude never crosses 0 dB, there is no gain crossover and PM is undefined.
fix: Say that if a 0 dB crossing exists, PM is read there; otherwise PM is undefined even though GM may be infinite.
